title: Intermittent WAN Degradation — Operator Runbook for Private Deployments
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:

This runbook describes detection, mitigation, and post-incident steps for intermittent WAN degradation affecting Redwood Private deployments (VPC-connected or on-prem control plane bridges). It focuses on preserving SLOs, minimizing model-serving disruption, safe traffic steering, and safe rollback/upgrade behavior when WAN links fluctuate.

Scope:
- Applies to private deployments with hybrid control planes (VPC+edge), air-gapped bridges, and VPC-peered tenant topologies.
- Covers symptoms related to intermittent increased latency, packet loss, asymmetric routing, and short network partitions (seconds to minutes).
- Not intended for full datacenter failure: see Disaster Recovery runbooks for regional failover.

Owner & escalation:
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments / Field Operations (oncall: #pod-privops)
- Secondary owner: eng-sre (oncall: #sre-oncall)
- Pager: +1-555-0102 (privops)
- If customer impact > 10% of tenant requests or SLA breach suspected, escalate to Engineering Manager (Elena Martinez) and Customer Success lead (Ravi Kumar).

SLOs and impact thresholds (operational):
- Healthy: control-plane request p95 <= 250 ms, tokenized inference p95 <= 400 ms.
- Degraded: sustained >20% increase above baseline latency OR packet loss >3% for >= 60s.
- Critical: sustained packet loss >10% or periodic disconnects causing >1% of requests to error for >= 5 min.

Signals & detection (alarms):
1) Automated alerts:
   - Telemetry: control-plane RPC error-rate spike, model-serving tail-latency increase, and KV-cache miss storm.
   - Network sensors: BGP flaps, interface errors, RTT jump, interface input errors.
   - Ingest: increased retransmits and TLS session resets reported by edge proxies.
2) Customer reports: elevated 5xx errors, streaming timeouts.
3) Synthetic checks: cross-region / tenant health checks failing intermittently.

Immediate triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm alarm: check telemetry dashboards (Redwood Console -> Private Deployments -> Tenant X -> Latency & Errors).
2) Verify scope: identify affected tenants, control-plane nodes, and AZs. Use redwood-ctl status --tenant <id> --scope network to list impacted routes.
3) Capture artifacts:
   - redwood-ctl trace capture --duration 120s --include=network,proxy,kv
   - tcpdump on affected interface: sudo tcpdump -i <iface> -w /tmp/wan-issue.pcap (rotate after 2 min)
4) Check provider signals: cloud provider network health dashboard, router BGP peer status, WAN provider NOC bulletins.

Tiered response (action matrix):
- Tier 1 (Transient blips, <60s): monitor and annotate incident. Increase sampling on traces but avoid changing config.
- Tier 2 (Degraded, 60s–10m): apply graceful traffic throttles and reroute noncritical traffic. Notify CS for impacted tenants.
- Tier 3 (Critical, >10m or SLA risk): execute traffic steering to alternate control-plane region or enable degraded-mode serving. Consider controlled rollback of recent changes.

Immediate mitigations (playbook):
1) Reduce noisy background traffic:
   - Apply egress rate limit for telemetry-heavy collectors to 20% of baseline: redwood-ctl policy apply --path /telemetry/ingest --egress-cap 20%
   - Temporarily disable scheduled large-model preloads (model prefetch) via config flag: set config.model_prefetch=false for affected clusters.
2) Prefer local inference paths:
   - If model artifact exists locally on edge nodes, shift routing to local-only mode: redwood-ctl route set --tenant <id> --prefer-local true
   - Confirm KV cache hits: redis-cli -h <kv-host> INFO and check keyspace hits/misses.
3) Reroute control-plane to alternative region (safe fallback):
   - Only for tenants with fallback allowed in config.json: if fallback_enabled == true then execute: redwood-ctl failover start --from-region A --to-region B --tenant <id>
   - Use canary traffic percentage (start 5%) and watch error rates for 3 minutes.
4) Switch to degraded-mode policy for latency-sensitive endpoints:
   - Replace full response streaming with chunked summary responses (low-bandwidth fallback).

Safe traffic steering checklist (detailed):
1) Authorization & customer consent: verify tenant contract allows cross-region steer and notify CS with template (see templates section).
2) Capacity check: ensure target region has at least 1.5x measured peak qps reserved for tenant during failover window. Use capacity query: redwood-ctl capacity query --region B --reserve 1.5x --tenant <id>
3) Consistency considerations: model versions pinned? If target region runs a quantized variant, enable quality guardrail: redwood-ctl quality-check --model <model-id> --baseline <tenant-prompt-set>
4) KV cache warmup: pre-warm top-1000 keys with redwood-ctl cache prewarm --keys-file top_keys.txt --region B
5) Monitor: increase tracing to p100 sampling for the tenant during steer.

Model-serving and KV cache considerations:
- Avoid simultaneous model hot-swap during network instability. Hot-swap increases remote fetches and can amplify traffic.
- If large model layers are fetched over WAN, defer model downloads; prefer fallback quantized variants located locally.
- KV cache eviction policy: if eviction storms occur, throttle write-back via circuit breaker config: set config.kv.circuit_breaker_window=30s

Upgrade & rollback safety guidance (when WAN is unreliable):
- Postpone planned upgrades for control-plane or model hot-swap until link stability >= 30 min.
- If an upgrade caused the issue: perform incremental rollforward to previous stable build per the orchestrated-rollforward-and-customer-safeguards playbook.
- Rollback checklist:
  1) Verify stored artifacts and signatures: gpg --verify <artifact>.sig <artifact>
  2) Initiate controlled rollback targeting 10% of nodes as canary: redwood-ctl deploy rollback --target-percent 10 --reason "WAN_degradation"
  3) Monitor service-level metrics for 5 minutes before widening.

Customer communication templates (shortened):
- Initial alert (CS -> customer): "We are investigating intermittent network disruptions affecting inference latency for your tenant. Our team has applied traffic isolation measures and will notify you with updates every 15 minutes."
- Failover notification: "We are proactively steering traffic to an alternative control plane in <region>. You may observe brief consistency artifacts for pinned model versions. Estimated mitigation time: 30–45 minutes."

Post-incident actions (before incident close):
1) Collect all artifacts: pcaps, redwood-ctl traces, probe results, BGP logs, provider tickets.
2) Conduct a 30-min blameless incident review within 72 hours. Include: timeline, mitigation effectiveness, customer impact, and recommended preventive work.
3) Recommended follow-ups (backlog items):
   - Implement adaptive telemetry sampling to prevent noisy collectors from amplifying WAN saturation.
   - Add health-check that tracks asymmetric packet loss and route divergence.
   - Create automation to prewarm KV cache for tenants with fallback flags.

Runbook validation tests (quarterly):
- Synthetic scenario: inject 5% packet loss on control-plane interface for 5 minutes and validate:
  - automated alert triggers,
  - runbook mitigations complete without human-only steps within 10 minutes,
  - customer notification template is sent by CS automation.
- Chaos test: scheduled WAN flaps (BGP withdraw/announce) in staging for 3 AZs. Validate canary failover and rollback timeline.

Appendix: sample troubleshooting commands and expected outputs:
- Quick health checks:
  - redwood-ctl status --verbose --tenant <id>
  - curl -sS https://private-ctrl.<region>.internal/health | jq .
  - iperf3 -c <peer> -t 10 (target throughput / latency)
- Adjust iptables to drop 1% traffic for test: sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem loss 1%
- Capture example edge proxy error: tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/edge-proxy.log | grep "upstream reset"

Customer requirements summary (minimums for predictable private behavior):
| Category | Minimum requirement | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| WAN SLA | 99.95% with jitter < 30 ms p95 | Stable link reduces transient failovers |
| Layer 2/3 MTU | 1450–9000 (consistent across path) | Avoids fragmentation for model artifact streaming |
| BGP | Static or BGP with eBGP timers >= 3s and graceful restart | Prevents rapid flaps that trigger control-plane failover |
| KMS latency | <= 150 ms p95 to KMS endpoints | Key operations should not be intermittently slow |
| Local storage | 400 GB free on edge nodes (per model pool) | Allows local model replica and cache warmup |
